verdict.rationale: GitBook documents its own block-based visual editor with Markdown support and custom blocks, so writers can add structured components such as updates and interactive API blocks without HTML. Community users also confirm Markdown support. However, none of the specific components named in the story are evidenced, and MDX is never mentioned. missing for 10: explicit evidence of tabs, callouts/hints, code groups and steps blocks, MDX authoring support, Markdown syntax for those blocks in Git-synced files, independent hands-on corroboration of rich-component authoring.

support.subject: As a technical writer, I author pages in Markdown/MDX with rich components — tabs, callouts, code groups, steps — without writing custom HTML

citations.quote: GitBook’s AI-native visual editor makes it easy to write, review, and publish technical content — with Markdown, real-time collaboration, version control, and Git workflows built in
An updates block lets you add a changelog to any page
let your users test endpoints right on the page with interactive blocks
